rounds.proof_sketch: The removed __syncthreads() creates a race between warps 0-3 reading shared_sum[128-255] and warps 4-7 writing those locations. With stride=128 in first reduction iteration, thread 0 (warp 0) reads shared_sum[128] written by thread 128 (warp 4). Race manifestation depends on warp scheduling timing, not input values.
rounds.survival_reason: This is a race condition bug that is timing-dependent rather than value-dependent. The race occurs when warp 0 starts the reduction loop before warp 4 has completed writing to shared memory. However, modern NVIDIA GPUs have aggressive warp scheduling that often executes warps in near-sequential order, masking this bug. Additionally, memory write latency may complete before cross-warp reads occur in practice. Since 112 random seeds all passed bitwise, the hardware timing consistently hides this bug. No input value pattern can force different warp scheduling behavior.
rounds.kill_strategy: This mutant is unkillable through value-level testing alone. The bug is a race condition dependent on GPU hardware scheduling, not input values. To catch this, one would need either: (1) stress testing with thousands of runs on the same input, (2) testing on different GPU architectures with different schedulers, or (3) using race detection tools like cuda-memcheck --tool racecheck.
rounds.recommendations: Race condition mutants from __syncthreads() removal require non-deterministic stress testing beyond single-value comparison. Consider adding a 'race_stress' test mode that runs each test case 100+ times and checks for ANY failure. Also, static analysis tools or formal verification should flag missing synchronization barriers as higher-priority issues that may escape differential testing.
